findings.F1: Over the next day, a coin rises more than its normal drift after a large down day, by an amount that grows with the fall. The fall is that day's return divided by the coin's 30-day volatility. In the lowest decile (mean -1.77 volatilities) the next day ends +0.63 % above drift (t 4.19, 1524 cases, 59 % up). The second-lowest decile (mean -0.88) ends +0.29 % above drift (t 2.48, 1523). The middle and upper deciles end between -0.30 % and +0.04 %.
findings.F2: The rebound comes only from down days. On down days, the next day's volatility-scaled return falls as the day's scaled return rises: slope -0.064 (t -3.06, 7529 cases). On up days there is no matching effect: slope +0.018 (t 0.98, 7691 cases). Over all days the slope is -0.026 (t -2.75, 15220 cases).
findings.F3: Grouping by the raw daily return gives the same result. Days in the lowest quintile of a coin's own daily returns are followed by +0.45 % above drift the next day (t 4.63, 3450 cases). The other quintiles are followed by -0.20 % to -0.01 %.
findings.F4: The rebound is short-lived. On the 2-day grid, the lowest quintile of the scaled day return is followed by +0.55 % over 2 days (t 2.88, 1500). On the 3-day grid it is +0.23 % over 3 days (t 0.80, 1002), so nothing is added after the first day.
findings.F5: The rebound is uneven across coins and years. Slope t by coin is -3.91 for XMR and between -1.35 and +0.10 for the other five. By year the slope t is -2.47 in 2018, -3.25 in 2020 and -2.56 in 2023, but +1.14 in 2024 and +0.32 in 2025.
findings.F6: The rebound's size is large against costs. The lowest-decile rebound of +0.63 % in one day is about 3.3 times the 0.19 % round trip this backtest charged.
findings.F7: Saturdays stand out, but only as a calendar condition with no graded form. Saturday's daily return beats the other days by 0.39 % (+0.335 % against -0.056 % above drift; Welch t 4.26; 2484 Saturdays; 54.7 % up). The gap is positive in all 6 coins (t 0.34 to 2.67) and in 6 of 8 years. It is not graded by the prior day's return or by volatility: by volatility tercile it is +0.44 %, +0.01 % and +0.27 %.
findings.F8: The tested breakout distance shows no grading on either side of the 90-day high. Closes 0 to 5 % above the high are followed by -0.12 % above drift over 5 days (t -0.14, 120 cases). Closes 5 to 15 % above it are followed by +1.91 % (t 0.73, 50 cases). Below the high, the slope of the 5-day return on the distance has t 0.43 (3244 cases).
findings.F9: The book's worst days follow the coin's own rises. On the decile of the book's largest daily losses (mean -0.64 %), the coin had risen +1.40 % the day before. Over all days, the book earned 0.016 % a day against the coins' 0.07 % to 0.16 %, so it kept little of the market's rise.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's fall on a day, measured against its own volatility over the previous 30 days, the more the coin rises over the next day.
ideas.consequence: After a sharp down day a trader should favour a long for the following day, larger the deeper the fall, and refuse a short that bets on the fall continuing.
ideas.name: next-day rebound after sharp falls
